purpose: Test whether registered M4 opportunity can safely refine the validated reward-variance OARS-v2 proposer without sacrificing either component of its proposal utility.

development_evidence.historical_corpus: The 20 authenticated OARS confirmatory arms containing 1280 eight-candidate decisions.
development_evidence.live_identity_corpus: The authenticated 64-decision failed M4-Rescue qualification ledger, used only to verify exact reward-variance proposer replay and no-action behavior in its FIFO steady state.
development_evidence.exploratory_boundary: The policy and thresholds below were chosen after exploratory inspection of these data. This replay is an internal development qualification, not an independent efficacy estimate or confirmatory test.

policy.name: m4_shield
policy.base_proposer: The exact OARS-v2 reward_variance_risk proposal over the authenticated eight-group frontier.
policy.candidate_set: The authenticated eight-group controlled frontier reconstructed from controller-ordered lifecycle events.
base_objective_order: maximize summed reward variance among imminent-expiry groups
choose the lexicographically smallest ordered group-ID tuple
shield_feasibility: Retain at least two of the four base-proposal groups.
Keep selected valid actor tokens within [0.98, 1.02] times FIFO tokens using the existing ceil/floor integer boundary.
Match the base proposal's imminent reward-variance sum within the declared absolute tolerance.
Match the base proposal's total reward-variance sum within the declared absolute tolerance.
shield_objective_order: choose the lexicographically smallest ordered group-ID tuple
policy.actuation_rule: Enact the best feasible shield batch only when its imminent-expiry registered L1 exceeds the base proposal by more than the declared tolerance; otherwise return the base proposal exactly.
policy.imminent_definition: A group is imminent when start_weight_version + max_staleness_versions <= current_learner_version. The replay uses max_staleness_versions=1.

interpretation_boundary: Because this corpus informed the policy and gates, a pass establishes deterministic feasibility and retrospective proxy behavior only.
The failed-live ledger is used for runtime proposal identity and negative-control behavior, not efficacy.
No terminal benchmark, training-quality endpoint, wall-time benefit, or causal downstream effect is tested here.
Any live systems qualification or randomized quality acquisition requires a separately frozen protocol and explicit authorization.
